attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: Uses his own phrasing and keeps the 26-month window from the title. It is a firm statement about the present state of AI, so observation is the right kind. The rhetorical framing does not hide the testable core.

contract.note: The plain reading takes 'what ails' from the post's own list (reliability, hallucinations, toxicity) and treats 'resolve' as eliminating these problems. That is an ordinary reading. Leaving out alignment narrows the claim and does not stretch it against him. No source claims the problems were resolved, so the result does not depend on the reading.

evidence.note: OpenAI said in March 2023, within the period, that GPT-4 still hallucinates and is not fully reliable. This is a company disclosure, but it admits a weakness rather than promoting the company.
Google admitted in late May 2024 that AI Overviews gave inaccurate answers, days before the post. This shows reliability problems were still present.
Stanford's independent study (May 2024) found that commercial legal AI tools marketed as hallucination-free hallucinated 17–34% of the time.
Shows hallucinations were reduced, but the same passage calls them still a real issue. Under the contract, partial progress is not resolution.

reviews.rationale: Leading developers' own disclosures (OpenAI 2023, Google May 2024) and an independent Stanford evaluation (May 2024) show flagship deep-learning systems still hallucinated and were unreliable as of the post date. The only counterevidence (e4) shows progress, not resolution. The toxicity part has no specific evidence, but the hallucination and reliability evidence is enough to show the problems were not resolved.
